questions.prompt: A small conditional handles a closed, stable set. What justifies adding interchangeable policy objects?

options.label: Keep the simple conditional until an actual change axis justifies extra indirection.
Replace every conditional because more pattern names always improve design.
Apply a minimum pattern count based on the developer’s seniority.

questions.explanation: Complexity needs an actual variation/ownership reason, not a title or count.

questions.prompt: Two interchangeable shipping policies must preserve what?

options.label: Preserve accepted inputs, returned values and errors across every strategy and caller.
Return zero for invalid input in one policy to simplify its callers.
Only preserve the class name; units and errors can change silently.

questions.explanation: A common interface name does not establish behavioral substitution.

questions.prompt: The provider gives decimal string 12.50 and currency USD; the caller requires integer cents and currency. What should the adapter do?

options.label: Convert 12.50 USD to 1250 cents under an explicit currency/unit contract; reject ambiguous input.
Drop the currency and pass numeric 12.50 as if it were 1250 cents.
Turn missing or invalid input into zero without exposing failure.

questions.explanation: Validation, currency, precision and error states belong in the declared translation contract.

questions.prompt: A logging wrapper surrounds an effectful operation. What caller contract must be reviewed?

options.label: Invoke the underlying operation once and preserve its result or exception; define instrumentation failure policy separately.
Catch every exception and return success so logs remain quiet.
Retry secretly inside logging so one visible call always produces an outcome.

questions.explanation: Wrapping can change effect count, error behavior and ordering; instrumentation failures need a separate policy.

questions.prompt: The DI container constructs one shared service instance safely. What remains?

options.label: Check shared-state synchronization and dependency scope; one construction does not make the instance safe.
Construction safety proves all mutable state is safe across requests.
Store request/tenant state globally because the service exists only once.

questions.explanation: Container resolution safety does not make the instance’s state thread-safe or repair captured dependency scopes.
